plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms with golden stamens. The flowers open in the cool, quiet depths of winter, when most other plants are dormant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring, with peak bloom in midwinter (December to March)
plants.location: Southern Japan and the temperate gardens of the southeastern United States, such as Georgia and the Carolinas
plants.funFact: Tea comes from a close relative, Camellia sinensis. Camellia japonica seeds are pressed into prized camellia oil, which has long been used in Japan for hair care and for protecting tools.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic flower head up to 30 cm across, ringed with silky pink bracts around a crown of fuzzy centers. It grows on rugged fynbos slopes and is South Africa's national flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowers also seen through midsummer. Blooms vary by region and cultivar.
plants.location: Western Cape fynbos of South Africa
plants.funFact: Proteas are ancient flowering plants that date back tens of millions of years. They evolved to survive fire, and some resprout from underground woody lignotubers.

plants.name: Eucalyptus ficifolia
plants.description: A compact Western Australian tree that bursts into dense clusters of fluffy flowers in midsummer. Nectar-feeding birds and bees visit the blooms constantly.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, from about December to March in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southwestern Western Australia, widely planted in Perth and across southern Australia
plants.funFact: The petals are fused into a cap called an operculum, which pops off as the flower opens. The color comes from the stamens, which are the showy part of the flower.
